text: Which one of the following lanthanoids does not form $MO_{2}$? [M is lanthanoid metal]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Lanthanoids mainly show the +3 oxidation state; the +4 state, needed for an oxide $\mathrm{MO}{}_{2}$, is shown by Ce, Pr, Nd, Tb and Dy.

Pr ($4f^{3}6s^{2}$), Nd ($4f^{4}6s^{2}$) and Dy ($4f^{10}6s^{2}$) are therefore able to form $\mathrm{MO}{}_{2}$.

Yb ($4f^{14}6s^{2}$) shows +2 ($\mathrm{Yb}{}^{2+}$, $4f^{14}$) and +3 ($\mathrm{Yb}{}^{3+}$, $4f^{13}$). Reaching +4 would need removal of another electron from the nearly full 4f subshell, which requires very high energy, so Yb does not show +4 and does not form $\mathrm{YbO}{}_{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text:
For a chemical reaction A + B ⇌ C + D

($\Delta _{r}H^{\Theta }$ = 80 kJ mol$^{-1})$ the entropy change $\Delta _{r}S^{\Theta }$ depends on the temperature T (in K) as $\Delta _{r}S^{\Theta }$ $= 2T (J K^{-1}$mol$^{-1})$.

Minimum temperature at which it will become spontaneous is $___________ K. ($Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, $\Delta G^{\circ }=\Delta H^{\circ }-T\Delta S^{\circ }$

For a reaction to be spontaneous

$\Delta G^{\circ }<0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta H^{\circ }-T\Delta S^{\circ }<0$

$\Rightarrow$ $T>\frac{\Delta H^{\circ }}{\Delta S^{\circ }}$

$\Rightarrow$ $T>\frac{80000}{2T}$

$\Rightarrow$ $2T^{2} > 80000$

$\Rightarrow$ $T^{2} > 40000$

$\Rightarrow$ T > 200

The minimum temperature to make it spontaneous is 200 K.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text: 224 mL of $SO_{2(g)}$ at 298 K and 1 atm is passed through 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH solution. The non-volatile solute produced is dissolved in 36g of water. The lowering of vapour pressure of solution (assuming the solution is dilute) (P${}_{(H_{2}O)}^{o}$ = 24 mm of Hg) is x $\times$ $10^{-2} mm$ of Hg, the value of x is $___________. ($Integer answer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
moles of $SO_{2} =$ $\frac{224}{22400}$ = 0.01

moles of NaOH = molarity × volume (in litre)

= 0.1 × 0.1

= 0.01 moles

The balanced equation is

$SO_{2} + 2$NaOH $\to$ $Na_{2}SO_{3} + H_{2}O$

$\therefore$ Here NaOH is limiting Reagent.

2 mole NaOH produces 1 mole $Na_{2}SO_{3}$

0.01 mole NaOH produces
$\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ 0.01 mole $Na_{2}SO_{3}$

$\therefore$ Moles of $Na_{2}SO_{3} = 0.005$ mole

$Na_{2}SO_{3}$ $\to$ $2Na^{+} + SO_{3}^{2-}$

van’t Hoff factor (i) = 3

Moles of $H_{2}O =$ $\frac{36}{18}$ = 2 moles

According to Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure :

$\frac{P_{H2O}^{o}-P_{S}}{P_{H2O}^{o}}=\frac{in_{Na2SO3}}{n_{H2O}+in_{Na2SO3}}$

[ $n_{Na_{2}SO_{3}}$ << $n_{H_{2}O}$ ]

$\frac{P_{H2O}^{o}-P_{S}}{P_{H2O}^{o}}=\frac{in_{Na2SO3}}{n_{H2O}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{24-P_{S}}{24}=\frac{3\times 0.005}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $24 – P_{S} = 0.18$

$\Rightarrow$ $P_{S} = 23.82$

Lowering in pressure ($\Delta$P) = 0.18 mm of Hg

$= 18 × 10^{–2} mm$ of Hg
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

text:
A homogeneous ideal gaseous reaction $AB_{2(g)}⇌A_{(g)}+2B_{(g)}$ is carried out in a 25 litre flask at 27${}^{\circ }$C. The initial amount of $AB_{2}$ was 1 mole and the equilibrium pressure was 1.9 atm. The value of $K_{p}$ is x $\times$ $10^{-2}$. The value of x is $_________. ($Integer answer)

[$R = 0.08206 dm^{3}$atm $K^{-1}$mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


[p = Total pressure at equilibrium = 1.9 atm]

Now, at equilibrium pV = (1 + 2x)RT

$\Rightarrow 1+2x=\frac{pV}{RT}=\frac{1.9\times 25}{0.082\times 300}=1.93$

[V = 25 L, R = 0.082 L atm mol$^{-1} K^{-1} T = 300 K$]

$\Rightarrow x=\frac{1.93-1}{2}=0.465$

$\Rightarrow K_{p}=\frac{p_{A}\times p_{B}^{2}}{p_{AB2}}\Rightarrow \frac{\left (\frac{x}{1+2x}p\right )\times \left (\frac{2x}{1+2x}p\right )^{2}}{\left (\frac{1-x}{1+2x}p\right )}$

$=\frac{4x^{3}\times p^{3}}{(1+2x)^{3}}\times \frac{(1+2x)}{(1-x)\times p}=\frac{4x^{3}\times p^{2}}{(1+2x)^{2}\times (1-x)}$

$=\frac{4\times (0.465)^{3}\times (1.9)^{2}}{(1+2\times 0.465)^{2}\times (1-0.465)}=0.7285$ atm

$=72.85\times 10^{-2}$ atm $\simeq 73\times 10^{-2}=x\times 10^{-2}$

$\therefore$ $x=73$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift
